### Orchestrator · Question

> Owner decision (2026-09-28): commits keep the standard the history rewrite set, and the owner signs off every commit that reaches the main history: 'Signed-off-by: mick <sirmick@gmail.com>', added by the orchestrator at merge (git rebase --signoff on the branch, git commit -s on the merge). Main checkout, docs only, don't stage; run doccheck; answer on this thread with the paths.

### Architect · Answer

Event: `e869dd4bd68ceb79bfb8f72247a0945f` · 2026-09-28T09:50:11Z

> Done (main checkout, unstaged): CONTRIBUTING.md, .wash/SWARM.md.
> 
> CONTRIBUTING.md#commits is now the one definition, and it matches the log:
> - Subject `<component>: <what>`, in the book's voice, lower case after the colon (names keep their case), no final full stop, with a real example. No fixed length, because the log keeps none: over the last 400 commits the median subject is 65 characters, p90 88, max 123. It stays one line, and shorter is better.
> - A body giving the reason, wrapped at about 72 columns, which is what recent bodies mostly keep.
> - One logical change per commit; every commit builds and passes its tests.
> - No process bookkeeping: no package IDs, question numbers, thread names, review labels, and no WIP, fixup or fix-round commits in the main history (fold them before the merge).
> - `Owner decision: ...` for an owner's call.
> - AI work: a `Co-Authored-By` trailer naming the model.
> - A DCO sign-off on every commit; for agent work, the owner's, added at merge.
> The AI disclosure section now points to the Co-Authored-By trailer instead of `Assisted-by:`.
> 
> SWARM.md: the commit bullet is now a link to CONTRIBUTING.md#commits plus what is agent-only: the plan_accept trailers on the merge commit (Plan-Node, QA, Gates, Reviewed-by), and the owner's sign-off, which the orchestrator adds at merge (`git rebase --signoff`, `git commit -s`). Rule 10 is unchanged.
> 
> Checks: doccheck exit 0, mdbook build docs exit 0. The package worktrees (k7, b2, s2) still carry the old CONTRIBUTING.md until they rebase.
